pinev: Five Mile Hill crest, named in the 1900 Tribune; Baty's 90-ft shaft was sunk from the crest. Crest is the highest point of the dune mass south of the harbour on 2016 Michigan 1 m lidar (237.7 m).
'Just back of the summit' (Grand Rapids Herald 1900), i.e. the landward (east) side of the crest, within the 250 m ring.

Five Mile Hill named as the dune on the state park's east boundary (WPA 1941); name still in use 1934. On lidar the mass has two knobs: 226 m at 43.0561,-86.2413 right above the park and the 237.7 m summit 320 m east, joined by a saddle near 205 m; the 400 m ring covers both.

The Grand Haven city water storage tanks stood on Five Mile Hill (Muskegon Chronicle 1932). On 2016 lidar a round levelled pad about 32 m across sits on the summit at 232 m (43.0564,-86.2371) with a second small pad just S and an access road winding up: the tank site. Pin moved onto it (about 55 m from the old crest pin); the 400 m ring is kept so the W knob stays inside.
The tank pad is in the NW¼ of sec 29 T8N R16W (BLM PLSS), where the 1912 Ottawa plat shows a 'City of Grand Haven' strip just S of the channel: city water-works ground.
Sanborn: two concrete reservoirs built 1912, 200 ft above the water works; the 1932 Chronicle only named them.

Naming caution: the 1912 tanks stood on 'Leggatt's Hill', 'the high city hill just off Lake Ave.' (Tribune 1912); the 1899 Tribune puts the cache 'in the hill immediately back of the light house', the same high ground; only the 1932 Chronicle calls the tank hill Five Mile Hill. Whether Leggatt's Hill and Five Mile Hill are one hill or the 1932 writer conflated them is unconfirmed (1912 Sanborn and plat labels being checked).
